scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Vlečenoto is a traditional folk dance from the Skopje region of North Macedonia.
It is documented in the ethnographic records of the 20th century, notably by researcher Mihailo Dimovski in 1977, as a specific regional variant of the Macedonian oro.
The dance reflects the local cultural identity of the Skopje valley's female population.
on_screen: Map: North Macedonia · Europe

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Vlečenoto is a social folk dance, performed during traditional gatherings and celebrations.
The name 'the dragged' highlights the specific physical connection to the land and the rhythmic style preferred by the women of the Skopje region.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is performed by women in a semicircle formation.
The movement is characterized by a medium-fast tempo where the dancers drag their feet along the ground.
This dragging motion is interspersed with jumps.
Watch for The Drag.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music for Vlečenoto is set in a 2/4 rhythm.

While specific instruments are not listed in the primary sources, it is typically accompanied by traditional Macedonian folk instruments common to the Skopje region, such as the gajda, kaval, or tapan, which provide the necessary pulse for the medium-fast movements.
The pulse is 2/4.
The music is defined by a steady 2/4 meter played at a medium-fast tempo, providing a consistent pulse for the dragging footwork and occasional jumps.

The setting is traditionally outdoors in a village square or during communal gatherings.
